llm_summary_material: Black holes: classify by mass — stellar-mass (3–100 M☉) vs supermassive (10⁵–10¹⁰ M☉) — and remember Hawking radiation means they evaporate, though solar-mass lifetimes (~10⁶⁷ yr) exceed the universe's age.

Coffee: process cherries within hours — washed (ferment 12–72 h, bright/floral), natural (dry 2–4 weeks, fruity but off-flavour risk if uneven), honey (partial mucilage, graded yellow/red/black) — then dry to ~11% moisture and medium-roast at 205–215 °C just after first crack.

EVs: modern era dates to the 2008 Tesla Roadster; expect ~250 Wh/kg lithium-ion, battery costs down from ~$1,100/kWh (2010) to under $140/kWh (2023), and match charging standard to region (CCS, GB/T, CHAdeMO), with 800 V architectures adding 200 km in ~15 min.

Internet: trace milestones — ARPANET's first message (29 Oct 1969), TCP/IP flag day (1 Jan 1983), DNS (1983), the Web (1989–91), commercial opening (1995), search/Wikipedia/iPhone (1998/2001/2007) — and note backbone fibre now exceeds 100 Tb/s per pair.

Photosynthesis: two stages — light reactions (thylakoids split water, yield ATP/NADPH) then Calvin cycle (RuBisCO fixes CO₂) — with field efficiency only ~3% and global fixation ~120 Gt C/yr; C4 plants win in hot climates.

Solar: PV efficiency runs 20–23% commercial (33%+ lab tandem), utility-scale LCOE ~$0.048/kWh (2021, down >80% since 2010), China makes ~80% of panels, and CSP with molten-salt storage uniquely delivers power after sunset.

Wind: siting dominates because power scales with the cube of wind speed; the Betz limit caps efficiency at 59.3% (modern turbines hit 45–50%), turbines cut in near 3 m/s and shut down near 25 m/s, and offshore capacity factors exceed 50%.
